title: Bullying is good and moral
summary: NH argues bullying is a natural force, with bullies as 'agents of nature' who expose weakness, and says zero-tolerance policies and victim morality leave people defenseless. He recounts being severely bullied until about age 14, when he saw a weak friend earn respect by retaliating and started fighting back every time himself. His advice is to become a 'venomous frog' with a strong identity, and a dog rather than a sheep.
claims: Bullies exist at every age and setting; life is a constant battle and bullies are simply adversaries
Naivety is the main reason people get targeted; bullying's real aim is to break down identity and self-worth
Bullying stems from a natural human drive to dominate that appears from early childhood and cannot be eradicated
Modern morality elevates the victim over the hero and does not breed strength
If you are bullied, the problem is you being bullyable; placing yourself at the center of the problem is what lets you escape it
Might makes right; violence is a viable method and strength is always the better recourse than weakness
NH was bullied throughout school until about age 14 because he was weak and wouldn't stand up for himself; he holds no resentment toward his bullies
Bullying either forges or breaks you, like tempering or shattering a sword
Most bullying is psychological; physical bullying is the easier kind to deal with
Bullies are not masterminds but 'agents of nature' following a drive to dominate, so their attacks shouldn't be taken personally
Bullies escalate from insults to physical attacks after testing whether you respond
Zero-tolerance policies make bullying worse; the only thing that stops a bully is fighting back with matching force
Reporting bullying to adults rarely helped him; the one time it stopped was when a teacher physically confronted the bully
In middle school, as the smallest and youngest, he was beaten by strangers, including two kids who broke his nose for fun
He saw an equally weak friend respected because he always retaliated, including stabbing a bully's hand with a fork; this changed his outlook
From then on he attacked anyone who bullied him; he lost every fight but each bully left him alone afterward, and he never had to fight after middle school
Make bullies pay a price; physical injuries heal but the self-worth lost by never standing up for yourself doesn't
Cyberbullying may be worse than physical bullying because you can't fight back physically
Don't excuse bullies with their home life or 'he secretly likes you'; your imperative is survival
Be a 'venomous frog': you need not be big or skilled, only willing to make attackers pay; his body didn't change, his intent did
He kicked a boy in the face who slapped a book out of his hand; disproportionate, but it never happened again
Confident body language and firing back insults deter bullies; showing fear marks you as prey
Bullying taught him at 14 that being cerebral wasn't enough and that he had to be able to defend himself
People never exposed to hardship are traumatized by minor or distant events
Weakness can never be turned into strength; making victimhood an identity makes you unbearable to good people and a target for predators
Sheep, wolves and dogs: be a dog that uses wolf-like power to protect others; never be a sheep
Power is a neutral tool; he uses his strength and confidence to shelter and help people rather than bully
